# RM brief — REDSTRIKE GROUP LIMITED (09556328)
*as of 2026-09-30 · research passes: 1*

**Decision: REFER** — set by CON-01 — Late filing of annual accounts; CON-03 — Pattern of late filing; CON-04 — Micro-entity accounts  
**Qualifies as a lead:** yes

## Summary

- REDSTRIKE GROUP LIMITED (company number 09556328) is an active private limited company incorporated on 23 April 2015, trading under SIC code 93199 and reporting as a micro-entity. It has 3 active officers out of 10 appointed ever, with no new appointments in the last 12 months. `[profile; officers]`
- No charges are registered against the company at any time, so its security position is clean and a first-charge facility could be offered subject to the remaining policies. `[SEC-02]`
- The most recent accounts, made up to 30 June 2025, were filed early on 31 August 2025, and the next accounts are not due until 31 March 2027 with nothing currently overdue. As at the 30 September 2026 review date, however, those figures are already 15 months old. `[AA filed 2025-08-31; profile; computed]`
- CON-01 is triggered: the accounts to 30 June 2024 were filed on 30 June 2025, 94 days after the statutory deadline, which points to weak administrative control. `[CON-01; AA filed 2025-06-30]`
- CON-03 adds a pattern concern: two accounts filings in the last three years were late — 94 days late on 30 June 2025 and 3 days late on 31 March 2024 — so this is more than an isolated lapse. `[CON-03; AA filed 2025-06-30; AA filed 2024-03-31]`
- CON-04 applies because the latest filing is micro-entity accounts, which disclose neither turnover nor profit and cannot support a serviceability assessment on their own. Management accounts covering the most recent 12 months must be obtained before any decision. `[CON-04; AA filed 2025-08-31]`
- On approach, treat this as a referral: the security position is clean, but ask for up-to-date management accounts and an explanation of the repeated late filings before progressing. `[CON-01; CON-03; CON-04; SEC-02]`
